question.text: Chapter V of the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations 2008 empowers SEBI, after due process, to impose against a defaulting intermediary (which may include a SIAO employing SIAs) which of the following penalties?

answer.text: Only monetary penalty - no right of suspension, cancellation or warning.
Only cancellation of certificate - intermediaries cannot be warned or suspended.
Warning, censure, prohibition from taking up new assignments, suspension of certificate, cancellation of certificate, or monetary penalty - depending on gravity.
Only criminal prosecution - SEBI has no administrative penalty power against intermediaries.

explanation.text: The Logic: Conceptually, regulator sanction frameworks against intermediaries are graded and proportionate. Chapter V of the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations 2008 is widely understood to provide a menu including warning, censure, prohibition from taking up new assignments, suspension of certificate, cancellation of certificate, and monetary penalty, with the chosen sanction depending on the gravity and recurrence of the default. The Trap: "Only monetary penalty", "only cancellation", and "only criminal prosecution" each collapse a graded regime into a single tool, which is inconsistent with proportionality and due process. SEBI does have administrative penalty powers in addition to any criminal route. Note: The Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) confirms that the SEBI Act empowers penalties and adjudication against defaulting intermediaries, but the specific "warning / censure / prohibition / suspension / cancellation / monetary penalty" Chapter V menu is not enumerated on the pages reviewed. The framing above is offered as general SEBI Intermediaries Regulations context, not a direct workbook citation.
